claim: The card clicks through magnetic section stops as you scroll — easing into each detent with a soft landing.

q1_defects.answer: No broken/blank states. Idle, play-3, and all control frames keep the full ship-quality card (brass header, blue dot, 3 grey rows, rounded panel) crisp and well-framed. No clipping, no slab.

q2_reads_as.answer: Reads as discrete section snapping: the card lands at distinct detent positions across idle->play-3 (steps up the frame) and the bounce-high frame shows a springy overshoot with a slight rotational squash + ovalized accent dot (the 'soft landing'). The detent behavior matches the claim.

q3_discoverable.answer: All four labeled controls change the frame sensibly: 'Sections' changes which detent the card lands on at the pinned scroll position (low lands lower, high lands higher), 'bounce' adds the springy overshoot, 'sharpness' and 'span' adjust the landing. A user dragging any slider sees a response.

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive: play deltas 10.28/10.27/10.33 show steady motion and all 4 controls are live (changed=true) with monotonic luma/banding shifts. No dead controls.
evidence: metrics: play-1 delta=10.28 play-2 delta=10.27 play-3 delta=10.33

q5_net.answer: A user would be PLEASED: 'it clicks into place at each section and gives a satisfying little bounce' — the snap reads, the card stays pristine, and every slider does something.

flags.note: The difference between sections-low and sections-high is modest (a small change in landing position); a touch more separation between detents would make the 'magnetic stops' effect more obviously dramatic.
flags.evidence: control: sections changed=true but small (low.luma=16.3 -> high.luma=16.1)
